nodeData.topic: Day 01 · Krishna's Questions to Nanda Maharaja
nodeData.note: SB 10.24.1–13 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Fresh from showing that the brahmanas' wives' love outweighs ritual, Krishna comes home to find his own father preparing a grand sacrifice to Indra, and questions him like a teacher: what is it for, whom does it please, is it scripture or only custom? Nanda argues that Indra deserves worship as the giver of rain, and Krishna begins his reply with the philosophy of karma. In the questions Maharaj explains that Indra's pride comes from his position, and that love for Vraja grows through service. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Govardhana-lila · Day 02 · The Vrajavasis Worship Govardhana

nodeData.note: SB 10.24.14–37 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Krishna argues from the karma-only view to stop the Indra sacrifice, and Maharaj turns each point on us: our own deeds and conditioned nature shape our chanting and our future, and we may lack even a sudra's qualities. Krishna then founds the worship of the cows, the brahmanas and Govardhana Hill, appears as the hill, and the class closes with questions on caste and karma in devotional life. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Picking up at text 14, Maharaj explains that after hearing Nanda Maharaja, Krishna deliberately argues from the karma-only point of view. Krishna never teaches a false philosophy for its own sake; here He arranges His words with one aim: to take away Indra's pride.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:57 (auto-transcript): “After hearing from his father, Nandan Maharaj, Krishna started speaking with an intention to provoke the anger of Indra. Krishna is not a teacher of karma, he is not a teacher he had condemned. Any philosophy, Krishna does not prove his supreme position.”

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Lord Krishna Lifts the Govardhana Hill
nodeData.note: SB 10.25.1–33 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Indra, blinded by pride, sends the clouds of universal destruction on Vraja, and Krishna lifts Govardhana Hill to shelter his devotees for seven days. Maharaj shows how anger and pride destroy intelligence, why trouble starts the moment we think "I know", why in difficulty we run only to Govinda, and how Indra became humble through humiliation. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.
